summary: Alberta register lists a 30 m steel lookout tower built 2003 and active; no source found describes its history, public access or current condition.

staffing.status: staffed, generally April to October (general Alberta description)

access.note: No source says the public may visit. The register codes access mode as drive. Alberta describes its lookout sites as isolated working sites.

events.note: Register Year Constructed for the steel tower.

evidence.supports: Towers were built on high hills in the boreal forest and raised the observer above any obstacles to vision

evidence.supports: Steel came into use in the 1920s and gradually took over from wood in tower building
evidence.quote: Introduced in the 1920s, steel increasingly replaced wood for tower construction.

evidence.supports: The province says its sites are picked for clear sightlines, so fires can be detected and reported
evidence.quote: are located where visibility is favourable to detect and report wildfires

evidence.supports: Alberta says each lookout site has an observer on watch, generally from April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.quote: majority of lookouts are staffed throughout the core fire season with the remainder staffed only during high hazard and risk.

evidence.supports: Alberta calls its lookout sites isolated and says staff need to be ready for a varied set of situations, including a run-in with a curious bear

corrections.why: The register has no access-level field. The pipeline derives 'closed' from ACTIVE=Y (pipeline/regional/alberta_wildfire.py lines 36-39 and 146-149). No source found says the site is closed or open to the public.

corrections.current: Active fire lookout, staffed March–October; it is the observer's seasonal home. No public access to the tower or cabin — please don't visit uninvited.
corrections.proposed: No source says the public may visit. The register codes access mode as drive.
corrections.why: The March–October dates, the 'seasonal home' wording and the visit warning come from the pipeline's ACCESS_NOTE template (alberta_wildfire.py lines 79-82), set on every active record. The register's fields do not contain them.

corrections.current: The present structure (Alberta Wildfire's year of construction).
corrections.proposed: Register Year Constructed for the steel tower.
corrections.why: The register field is Year Constructed. 'Present structure' is a pipeline gloss, not register text.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Alberta.ca says each lookout site is staffed by an observer, generally April to October. The 2015 Alberta Wildfire review says most lookouts are staffed through the core fire season and the rest only during high hazard and risk. The story reports both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register row gives type (Steel), year (2003), height (30.0 m), elevation (1101.3 m), map sheet 83G/03, active flag, access mode drive and weather station, and nothing else for this site. The brief's access 'closed' and the March-October staffing wording are pipeline inferences, not register fields; see corrections. Staffing in facts rests on Alberta's general description of all sites, and the 2015 review qualifies it. The 1912 photo caption in Lonely Lookouts ('Tree crawl lookout, Brazeau Forest, 1912') names a forest area, not this tower, and is left out of the story. A hiking site called Brazeau Lookout on peakery.com, reporting viewpoints near 1,900 to 2,000 m, is not confirmed to be this register point at 1,101.3 m and was not used. AllTrails Brazeau returned 403. Access is set to restricted for the same reason as Blackstone. No photo, fire or rental source was found.
